walkthrough:
**Count electron pairs around sulfur**

Look at the dot-and-cross picture. Sulfur is in the middle with two double bonds and one lone pair on top.

That means: $$2 \text{ bonding pairs } + 1 \text{ lone pair } = 3 \text{ electron pairs around S}$$

**Apply VSEPR to get electron arrangement**

Three pairs of electrons repel to be as far apart as possible. That gives a trigonal planar arrangement of electron pairs.

Remember, lone pairs repel more strongly than bonding pairs, so they squeeze the bond angle a little below $120^{\circ}$.

**Name the molecular shape from atoms only**

Shape is named from the positions of atoms, not lone pairs. We see only $\text{O-S-O}$, with the lone pair pushing them bent.

So $\text{SO}_2$ is bent, which Cambridge calls non-linear, with a bond angle of about $119^{\circ}$.

options.A: Linear would need only 2 electron pairs and no lone pair on S, like in $\text{CO}_2$. Here S has an extra lone pair that repels and bends the molecule, so it cannot be straight.
options.B: Correct. With 2 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, $\text{SO}_2$ has a bent or V-shaped arrangement of atoms. This is described as non-linear.
options.C: Pyramidal needs 3 bonding pairs plus 1 lone pair, like in $\text{NH}_3$. $\text{SO}_2$ has only 2 atoms bonded to S, so there are not enough atoms to make a pyramid.
options.D: Tetrahedral needs 4 electron pairs with no lone pair effect on shape, like in $\text{CH}_4$. $\text{SO}_2$ has only 3 electron pairs in total, so this is impossible.
